title: Complete coefficient field arithmetic
statement: Let $A$ be a complete DVR with fraction field $K$ and algebraically closed residue field $k$ (every nonconstant polynomial over $k$ has a root in $k$) of characteristic $p>0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $E/K$ be finite and let $A_E$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $k\to A_E/\mathfrak m_{A_E}$ is an isomorphism and $\mathfrak m_AA_E=\mathfrak m_{A_E}^{[E:K]}$. There exists a finite normal extension $N/K$ containing $E$ such that $N/E$ is separable. Here normal means splitting of every irreducible polynomial with a root, finite means finite-dimensional, and separable has its algebraic meaning [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. If $\operatorname{char}(K)=p$, then for every uniformizer $t$ of $A$ and every such $E$ there are a finite separable subextension $E_s/K$ inside $E$ and $r\geq0$ with $t^{1/p^r}\in E$ and $E=E_sK[t^{1/p^r}]$. The right side is the subfield generated by the displayed fields in $E$. No Epp solution is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, proof paragraph taking normal closure of the coefficient solution (details omitted there); Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, proof paragraph observing that every finite extension of k((t)) is a separable/uniformizer-root compositum.

proof.text: Put C=A_E. A DVR is a principal ideal domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so A is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal; being local and complete, A is a Nagata ring by lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata. Applying def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring to the prime (0) shows that A=A/(0) is N-2, so def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain, applied to the finite extension E/K, makes C a finite A-module; no separability of E/K is used. By lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal, C is a domain with fraction field E. The domain clause of lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product then says that C is a Noetherian local ring, complete for its maximal ideal m_C, and m_C is the only prime of C whose inverse image in A is m_A; in particular m_C contracts to m_A. Since dim A=1 by lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one, lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr applies with D=A, L=E and q=m_C: the subring {c/s : c,s in C, s not in m_C} of E is a DVR with fraction field E. As C is local, every s outside m_C is a unit of C, so this subring is C itself. Thus C is a complete DVR with fraction field E, finite over A, and A -> C is local. Hence k maps injectively into l=C/m_C; a finite list of A-module generators of C maps to a spanning list for l over k. Apply lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial to this finite field extension: the specified residue map k -> l is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09F8, first proof paragraph (integral closure finite over the Nagata ring B, a complete DVR, citing Algebra 032W and Remark 09EM); Tag 09GR for the residue-field conclusion.

proof.text: Choose uniformizers pi of A and z of C. The DVR unit-times-power lemma applied to the nonzero nonunit pi in C gives pi=v z^e for a unit v and e>=1. The finite A-module C is torsion free since C is a subring of E. Embed it in A^a by lem-per-finite-torsion-free-free-embedding; a DVR is a PID, so lem-weil-pbc-pid-submodule-finite-basis gives an A-basis b_1,...,b_d of C (transport the basis of its image back along the embedding). Reducing its unique coordinate expressions modulo pi gives a k-basis of C/pi C of size d.

source.place: Tag 09F8 omitted total-ramification calculation; Algebra Tag 00PD; More on Algebra Tags 0AUU and 0ASU.

proof.text: The b_i are also a K-basis of E. Indeed, each x in E is c/a with c,a in C and a nonzero. Write a=w z^j. Choosing h with eh>=j shows pi^h/a in C and therefore x in C[1/pi]. Thus E=C[1/pi]. Clearing powers of pi in a K-linear relation proves independence of the b_i, while localizing their A-linear expansions proves spanning. Consequently d=[E:K].

source.place: Tag 09F8 omitted total-ramification calculation; Algebra Tag 00PD.

proof.text: Since pi C=z^e C, filter C/pi C by the images of z^i C for 0<=i<=e. Multiplication by z^i identifies C/z C with z^i C/z^(i+1) C: surjectivity is the definition of the principal ideal, and cancellation in the domain C gives its kernel z C. This is k-linear using the residue map of step 1, so every successive quotient has dimension one over k. All filtered terms are subspaces or quotients of the finite-dimensional C/pi C. Repeatedly apply lem-trf-finite-dimensional-short-exact-dimension to the inclusions of successive filtered terms and their quotient maps. It gives dim_k C/pi C=e. Steps 2 and 3 therefore give e=d=[E:K] and m_A C=m_C^[E:K].

source.place: Tag 09F8, assertion that normal-closure extension is totally ramified: explicit length calculation.

proof.text: For the remaining equal-characteristic assertion assume char K=p, so char A=p. Apply lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists to A. Its coefficient subring Lambda satisfies Lambda intersect m_A=p Lambda=0 and maps isomorphically onto k. The inverse of this residue isomorphism gives a ring section s:k -> A. Fix the uniformizer t specified in the statement. Since A is complete for (t), lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation defines evaluation k[[T]] -> A with coefficients mapped by s and T mapped to t.

source.place: Tag 09F9, paragraph choosing k[[t]] -> A; Algebra Tag 032A(1); Tags 07NL and 07NN.

proof.text: Every a in A has a unique expansion sum_(i>=0) s(c_i)t^i. Construct c_0 as its residue, replace a by (a-s(c_0))/t in A, and repeat. For every N this recursion gives the required expansion modulo t^N; completeness and the evaluation formula of step 5 give the equality. For uniqueness, the first nonzero coefficient of a difference is a unit times its power of t: after removing that power, the remaining series has nonzero residue. This proves injectivity as well as surjectivity of the evaluation. Since every fraction in K becomes an element of A after multiplication by a power of t (the DVR unit-times-power lemma), the same argument gives unique Laurent expansions with only finitely many negative exponents.

source.place: Tag 09F9, k((t)) compositum paragraph: explicit expansion argument; Tags 00PD and 07NL.

proof.text: The field k is perfect: a root of X^p-c exists for every c in k, and it is unique since a field has no nonzero nilpotents. Group the Laurent expansion of x in K by exponents modulo p, and take p-th roots of its coefficients in k. This gives x=sum_(j=0)^(p-1) t^j y_j^p with y_j in K. Frobenius commutes with these sums because the identity for finite truncations holds modulo every t^N and A is separated. The valuations of nonzero terms t^j y_j^p have distinct residues j modulo p, so a sum of such terms cannot vanish: the term of least valuation has nonzero leading coefficient. Thus 1,t,...,t^(p-1) is a basis of K over K^p and [K:K^p]=p. Iterating the field identity K=K^p(t) gives K=K^(p^n)(t) for every n: raise it to p^i to obtain K^(p^i)=K^(p^(i+1))(t^(p^i)), and substitute successively.

source.place: Tag 09F9, expansion of the assertion about finite extensions of k((t)); explicit Frobenius grouping.

proof.text: For any intermediate field K subset F subset E, F/K is finite. The Frobenius isomorphisms F -> F^p and K -> K^p transport any K-basis of F to a K^p-basis of F^p, so [F^p:K^p]=[F:K]. The tower K^p subset K subset F is finite by degree multiplicativity, and therefore F/F^p is finite by the finite-intermediate-field lemma. Comparing the two towers from K^p to F gives [F:F^p][F:K]=[F:K]p. Since [F:K] is a positive integer, [F:F^p]=p.

source.place: Tag 09F9, k((t)) compositum paragraph; Fields Tag 09G9, applied to the two Frobenius towers.

proof.text: Let S be the separable algebraic closure of K in E. The separable-first lemma says S/K is separable and E/S is purely inseparable; both are finite by the finite-intermediate-field lemma. Apply lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower to obtain S=F_0 subset F_1 subset ... subset F_r=E, with F_i=F_(i-1)(alpha_i), alpha_i^p in F_(i-1), and [F_i:F_(i-1)]=p. Taking p-th powers of rational expressions in alpha_i shows F_i^p subset F_(i-1). Step 8 applied to F_i gives [F_i:F_i^p]=p, so degree multiplicativity forces F_i^p=F_(i-1). Iterating yields E^(p^r)=S. The case E=S gives the empty tower r=0 and the same equality.

source.place: Tag 09F9, k((t)) compositum paragraph; Fields Tags 030K, 09HI and 09G9.

proof.text: Put q=p^r. By lem-sfb-separable-powers-generate, S=K(S^q). Step 7 gives K=K^q(t), hence S=S^q(t), since K^q subset S^q. By E^q=S there is u in E with u^q=t. For x in E, write x^q in S=S^q(t) as a rational expression in t whose finitely many coefficients are q-th powers of elements of S. Taking those coefficient roots and replacing t by u gives y in S(u) with y^q=x^q; the denominator stays nonzero because its q-th power is the original nonzero denominator. Frobenius is injective in E, so x=y. Therefore E=S(u)=S K[t^(1/p^r)], with the required finite separable E_s=S contained in E. This argument works for each specified t; for r=0 one can simply take u=t.

source.place: Tag 09F9, explicit proof of the finite k((t))-extension compositum assertion; powers-generating Mathlib theorem.

proof.text: Construct a normal overfield next. If char K=0, take any finite normal overfield N/K containing E by lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension. The characteristic-zero clause of lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable, applied to N/E, says that every element of N is separable over E, as required. These two characteristics exhaust the cases: a positive characteristic of K must equal p because A injects into K and has a nonzero residue field of characteristic p.

source.place: Tag 09F8, omitted normal-closure separability; Fields Tags 09DT and 030K.

proof.text: In characteristic p use S,u,q from steps 9-10. The finite-Galois-receiving lemma for the single extension S/K gives a finite normal separable T/K and a K-embedding tau:S -> T. Work in an algebraically closed overfield Omega containing E. Extend the map tau(S) -> Omega, tau(s) |-> s, to an embedding T -> Omega by lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed. Here T/tau(S) is finite by the finite-intermediate-field lemma. Replace T by this image; it is now an actual subfield of Omega containing S, without changing its finite, normal or separable properties over K.

source.place: Tag 09F8 omitted normal-closure construction; Fields Tags 09DT, 0EXM and 09GU.

proof.text: The field K(u) is the splitting field of X^q-t: in Omega this polynomial is (X-u)^q, and its only root is u. It is nonconstant, also when q=1. Apply lem-sfb-splitting-field-finite-normal to get K(u)/K finite normal. Put N=T K(u) inside Omega. By lem-sfb-finite-normal-field-compositum it is finite normal over K, and it contains E=S K(u). Moreover N=E(T), since S subset T and E=S K(u). Every element of T is separable over K; lem-sfb-separable-generated-scalar-extension with base field M=E and U=T gives N/E separable. This completes the normal-overfield assertion in characteristic p. The residue and ramification assertions for E were proved in steps 1-4; the same argument also applies to N/E over the complete DVR C with residue k.

source.place: Tag 09F8 omitted normal-closure separability and total ramification; Fields Tags 09HU, 0BR3, 09H2 and 09HC.
